meal.name: MB3+ Ribeye Dinner
meal.workflow_md:
## Menu 3 portions · ~2 hr 5 min total · 26 May 2026 - Dish 1 — Reverse-Seared MB3+ Ribeye with Mushroom Finish - Dish 2 — Cannellini Bean, Tomato & Spinach Braise - Dish 3 — Charred Gruyère Cauliflower - Dish 4 — Warm Blueberry-Strawberry Compote ## T−Minus Timeline
TimeAction
T−125Pat steak completely dry on all surfaces; season with Diamond Crystal kosher salt; leave uncovered to temper at room temperature.
T−80Preheat oven to 250°F / 120°C.
T−65Steak onto rack over tray; into oven at 250°F / 120°C.
T−55Bean braise — heat oil over medium on Burner 1; add tomatoes (~300 g / ¾ tin); begin reduction.
T−45Remove frozen cauliflower from freezer; leave at room temperature to partially thaw.
T−40Add cannellini beans to braise; reduce to medium-low; simmer.
T−35Compote — frozen berries over low heat on Burner 2; reduce lightly until glossy (~10 min).
T−25Compote done; remove from heat; hold at room temperature. Fold spinach and parmesan into braise; move to very low heat on Burner 1; cover and hold. Pat cauliflower dry; into dry pan on Burner 2 at maximum heat (Phase 1: moisture cook-off).
T−23Check steak internal temp — if approaching 105–108°F / 40–42°C, monitor every 3 min.
T−20Steak at 112–115°F / 44–46°C; remove to rack to rest uncovered.
T−13Cauliflower charred on contact surfaces; transfer to heatproof dish (no cheese yet). Mushrooms into same dry pan on Burner 2 at maximum heat.
T−9Mushrooms cooked off and dry; remove. Add gruyère to cauliflower; butane torch to melt and colour (~60–90 sec). Wipe Burner 2 pan; add neutral oil.
T−7Oil smoking; begin steak sear — 75–90 sec first side (steak has rested 13 min).
T−5Flip steak — 45–60 sec second side; render fat edge 20 sec.
T−4Steak off pan. Return mushrooms; add parmesan; 30–40 sec; remove from heat.
T−3Check braise — loosen with hot water if over-reduced. Slice steak immediately.
T−0Plate and serve.
## Critical Path Steak reverse sear → 13-min rest → final sear → immediate slice and plate. Do not delay steak service for any other component. If timing slips: serve steak immediately; accept cauliflower with reduced char; loosen braise to order. ## Oven Sequencing & Heat Allocation 250°F / 120°C only — steak T−65 to T−20; no competing oven requirement. Cauliflower runs entirely on induction. Burner 1: braise active T−55 to T−25, then very low hold through service. Burner 2: compote (T−35 to T−25), cauliflower charring (T−25 to T−13), mushrooms (T−13 to T−9), steak sear (T−7 onward) — strictly sequential on the same burner. Cauliflower and mushroom cook-off cannot overlap; sear follows mushroom cook-off on the wiped, re-oiled pan. ## Holding Chain
ComponentHold StrategyMax HoldDrift RiskCorrective
SteakRack, uncovered13 minCarryover overshootBegin sear at T−7 without delay
Bean braiseCovered, very low heat, Burner 125 minOver-thickeningLoosen with 2–3 tbsp hot water; stir before serving
CauliflowerHeatproof dish, uncovered9 min post-torchCrust softeningBrief 10-sec torch pass restores surface texture
MushroomsPan edge, residual heat5 minMoisture weep20-sec reheat at high before parmesan addition
CompoteOff heat, in pan30 minNone materialNot required

dishes.name: Reverse-Seared MB3+ Ribeye with Mushroom Finish
dishes.summary: MB3+ ribeye brought to 112–115°F in a 250°F / 120°C oven, rested 13 min and seared hard in the mushroom pan, served with a parmesan-glossed frozen-mushroom finish alongside.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Reverse sear establishes uniform internal doneness before the final high-heat crust; mushroom and parmesan finish served alongside, not over, the steak. ## Yield & Timing Yield: 3 · Total: ~1 hr 20 min · Active: ~25 min · Oven: 250°F / 120°C ## Prep Phase 1. Pat steak completely dry on all surfaces including edges and fat cap. 2. Season with Diamond Crystal kosher salt on all surfaces. 3. Leave uncovered at room temperature 45–60 min before entering the oven. ## Active Cooking **Workflow summary:** Mushroom cook-off (Burner 2, T−13 to T−9) and steak sear (T−7 onward) are sequential in the same pan. Mushrooms must be fully cooked off, removed, and the pan wiped and re-oiled before the steak enters. Any residual moisture prevents crust formation. 1. Place steak on rack over a tray; into oven at 250°F / 120°C. 2. Check internal temp at T−23 (approx. 40 min). *If approaching 105–108°F / 40–42°C, monitor every 3 min.* 3. Pull at 112–115°F / 44–46°C. Carries to 119–125°F during rest; final sear raises centre to approx. 125–130°F / 52–54°C. Do not rely on elapsed time alone. 4. Remove to rack; rest uncovered. Begin sear at T−7. 5. Mushroom cook-off (Burner 2, from T−13): dry pan at high heat, 4–5 min without excessive stirring. *Primary cue: pan sounds dry — no sizzling water, only dry browning sounds.* Remove mushrooms; wipe pan. 6. Add 15 ml neutral oil to wiped pan; return to maximum heat. *Oil must be visibly smoking before steak enters.* 7. Sear: 75–90 sec first side without moving. *Release cue: steak lifts cleanly with deep even browning.* Do not force the flip. 8. Flip: 45–60 sec second side. Render fat cap on edge 20 sec. 9. Remove steak to board. Return mushrooms to pan; add parmesan; 30–40 sec to gloss. Remove. *Secondary doneness cue (pre-sear):* press centre lightly — if firm with significant resistance, shorten sear to 45–60 sec per side and skip the edge render. ## Holding & Assembly Rest on rack, uncovered. Begin sear at T−7 without delay. Slice immediately before plating — do not slice and hold. Spoon mushrooms alongside, not over, the steak. Serve steak partially over the bean braise. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
CriticalReverse sear overshoot — steak feels firm at centre; edges show grey before sear beginsUnrecoverable — shorten sear to absolute minimum; serve promptly
MajorSear crust failure — pale grey surface on contact; pan moisture audible as weak sizzle instead of hard searUnrecoverable for that side; re-sear opposite side aggressively; accept uneven crust
MajorMushroom moisture in sear pan — steak sizzles weakly and steams on contactRemove steak; fully dry pan; re-heat oil to smoking; return steak
MinorParmesan dominates beef at service — cheese aroma stronger than beefReduce parmesan on mushrooms; do not apply directly to sliced steak
## Adjustment Notes Taste sliced steak before adding finish salt — MB3+ fat amplifies salt perception; adjust only if under-seasoned. If crust softens during the rest-to-sear window, a 20-sec reflash in a dry pan at maximum heat recovers it. If the plate reads heavy, increase braise proportion per bite rather than adding acid to the steak.

dishes.name: Cannellini Bean, Tomato & Spinach Braise
dishes.summary: Tinned cannellini beans simmered in reduced crushed tomatoes with frozen spinach and parmesan, held covered on very low heat as the acid-balancing bed for the steak.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Thick tomato-cannellini braise providing the meal's acid balance — calibrated to support the steak, not compete with it. ## Yield & Timing Yield: 3 · Total: ~30 min · Active: ~15 min ## Prep Phase 1. Drain and rinse beans lightly. Some surface starch aids cohesion — do not rinse aggressively. ## Active Cooking 1. Heat oil over medium on Burner 1. 2. Add ~300 g tomatoes. Reduce over medium, stirring occasionally, until reduced by roughly one-third and *the surface coats a spoon lightly* — approx. 15 min. If tomato flavour reads full and deep before this point, hold back the remaining ¼ tin. 3. Add drained beans. Reduce to medium-low; simmer until cohesive and thick but beans hold their shape — approx. 15 min. 4. Fold in frozen spinach; wilt fully, 2–3 min. 5. Stir in parmesan off heat. Move to very low heat on Burner 1; cover and hold. ## Holding & Assembly Hold covered on very low heat on Burner 1 through service. At T−3: stir and check consistency — loosen with 2–3 tbsp hot water if tightened. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorUnder-reduced — liquid runs freely off a spoon; no bodyContinue reducing uncovered; remove lid completely
MajorOver-reduced — paste-like texture; beans compacting and beginning to break downAdd hot water 2 tbsp at a time; stir over low heat
MinorSpinach metallic dominance — vegetal flavour obscures the tomato-bean baseSmall splash of reserved tomato liquid or extra tbsp parmesan
## Adjustment Notes Add salt only after reduction completes — it concentrates with the liquid. If the braise reads flat after the hold, add the reserved ¼ tin of tomatoes and stir briefly over low heat. Thin with water only — oil at this stage breaks the emulsification.

designed_unvalidated.note: Cue: surface coats a spoon lightly; hold back remaining ¼ tin if flavour reads full early.
Cohesive and thick but beans hold shape.

dishes.name: Charred Gruyère Cauliflower
dishes.summary: Partially thawed frozen cauliflower dry-charred on induction at maximum heat, then topped with gruyère and torched to a bubbling, coloured finish.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Pan-charred on induction at maximum heat, finished with butane-torched gruyère — provides bitterness, char, and texture contrast with no oven conflict. ## Yield & Timing Yield: 3 · Total: ~20 min active · Equipment: induction Burner 2, butane torch ## Prep Phase 1. Remove cauliflower from freezer at T−45; leave at room temperature to partially thaw. 2. Pat dry at T−25 before placing in the pan. ## Active Cooking 1. At T−25: heat dry pan on Burner 2 to maximum heat. *Cue: a drop of water evaporates in under 1 sec.* 2. Add cauliflower dry; do not overcrowd. 3. **Phase 1 — Moisture cook-off (~2–3 min):** cauliflower will steam initially; wait until audible moisture fully subsides. 4. Add 15 ml neutral oil; toss briefly. 5. **Phase 2 — Charring (~5–7 min):** let florets sit in contact with the pan; turn only to expose uncharred surfaces. *Primary cue: edges deeply charred, centres yield to gentle pressure but hold shape.* 6. Season lightly with Diamond Crystal. 7. At T−13: transfer charred cauliflower to a heatproof dish (no cheese yet). Burner 2 is now free for mushrooms. 8. At T−9: distribute gruyère evenly over cauliflower; butane torch in slow passes 5–8 cm above the cheese until *fully melted, bubbling, and beginning to colour* — 60–90 sec. Serve within 9 min. ## Holding & Assembly Serve uncovered within 9 min of torching. Do not cover. If hold extends, a brief 10-sec torch pass over the set cheese restores surface texture. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorPan too cool or overcrowded — pale wet surfaces after 4 min; no audible dry searReduce quantity; increase heat; press florets against surface with spatula
MajorOvercrowded pan — water pooling beneath florets; no contact browning visibleCook in 2 batches; first holds uncovered while second finishes
MinorGruyère burns under torch — dark, bitter-smelling spots on cheese surfaceMove torch faster and further away; underlying cheese typically intact
## Adjustment Notes Finish cauliflower lightly with salt after torching, before serving. If texture has softened during the hold, a brief 10-sec torch pass restores the crust. Reduce gruyère to 25 g / 0.9 oz if the meal reads heavy.

dishes.name: Warm Blueberry-Strawberry Compote
dishes.summary: Frozen blueberries and strawberries warmed over low heat until glossy but still fluid, seasoned with a pinch of salt and held at room temperature as a light palate reset after the beef.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Warm, glossy berry compote serving as a light palate reset after the beef course — made at T−35, held at room temperature. ## Yield & Timing Yield: 3 · Total: ~10 min · Active: ~5 min · Holds 30 min at room temperature ## Prep Phase None required. ## Active Cooking 1. Add frozen berries to a small pan over low heat on Burner 2 at T−35. 2. Warm gently until *juices release and berries are fully thawed* — approx. 5 min. 3. Reduce lightly until *surface is glossy but mixture remains fluid, not jammy.* 4. Add one pinch Diamond Crystal. 5. Taste. Add sugar only if flavour reads flat or sharp. Remove from heat at T−25; hold at room temperature. ## Holding & Assembly Serve warm or at room temperature. Holds up to 30 min without quality loss. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MinorOver-reduced — jam-like body; skins wrinkling and separatingRemove from heat; add 2–3 tbsp water; stir briefly over low heat
## Adjustment Notes If the compote reads sweet and flat, increase the strawberry ratio or add a small squeeze of lime if available. Thin with water only if paste-like — do not reduce further once glossy.

designed_unvalidated.note: Cue: glossy surface, mixture still fluid, not jammy.
